observations.text: Fourth correction re-review. HEAD is now ea8f6d9, tree clean; argv: git status --porcelain -> exit 0, stdout empty. argv: git diff --stat 5843ed2 HEAD -> exit 0: crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs, crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs, crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/{resume.rs,mod.rs}, the ADR renamed to docs/adrs/ADR-092-review-app-resumed-scan-takes-over-plan-row-statuses.md, the feature briefs and run records, tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs. Three production crates and two acceptance files changed, so this round re-ran everything the earlier rounds ran plus a release check: nothing was reused.

Affected checks re-executed at HEAD ea8f6d9, each argv with its exit and result. (1) cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture: exit 0, 11 passed 0 failed. (2) cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store -p ports: exit 0, 265 passed 0 failed over 11 binaries. (3) cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins: exit 0, 39 passed 0 failed; this is the corrected command 6 and it now runs. (4) cargo xtask check-arch: exit 0, 'check-arch: OK (30 workspace members)'. (5) cargo test -p xtask: exit 0, 380 passed 0 failed over 20 binaries. (6) cargo check --release --workspace: exit 0, no error; the release build compiles with no ScanWriteSeam, no Mutex and no poisoned-lock path. (7) cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0, no warning anywhere in the workspace. (8) cargo test -p openlore-review-app: exit 0, 322 passed 0 failed over 22 binaries, every binary 'test result: ok'. No count moved from the previous round, which is what a behaviour-preserving refactor and a documentation correction should show.

All five findings are resolved, each in its own artifact. Design: docs/feature/fix-repos-read-across-resume/architecture.md:115 now reads 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins', which I ran at exit 0 with 39 passed; docs/product/architecture/ADR-001.md is gone and the decision is docs/adrs/ADR-092-review-app-resumed-scan-takes-over-plan-row-statuses.md. Release seam: crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs now carries scan_write as Mutex<ScanWriteSeam> under #[cfg(debug_assertions)] and as a plain Option<ScanWriteFault> under #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))], with a second admits_scan_write for the release build that reads the field straight off and calls the pure admits, so there is no lock and no StoreError::Database('scan write seam lock poisoned') on a release path at all; the BTreeSet import, the ScanWriteSeam struct and its impl are all gated, and the doc comments now say what each build carries. cargo check --release --workspace exits 0. Resume partition: crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs now holds one private Vec<(usize, Disposition)> with Disposition a private sum of ToRead, Carried, AlreadyRead and Skipped(CarriedSkip); to_read, carried, already_read, skipped and kept are all derived over that one sequence, so no two answers can name the same position by construction and the disjointness the count rests on is no longer a property-tested invariant but a structural one. resume_plan is a filter_map over the pure total disposition_of, and kept needs no sort because plan order is the sequence's own. Adopted properties: acceptance.md now records crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs::a_resume_keeps_as_read_exactly_the_rows_the_scan_already_read at line 449 and crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs::a_plan_reads_back_with_the_statuses_it_was_written_with at line 483, each with its stimulus, its expected observation, its user value and an honest caveat naming what it does not observe, so every test in the candidate now has one owner and the acceptance brief records sixteen locators.

The test edits of this round are the mechanical migration the refactor forces, and nothing is weakened. tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs changes verdict.to_read.clone() to verdict.to_read() and verdict.skipped to verdict.skipped(); tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:401-411 changes the same two field reads to method calls; crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs changes its own in-crate reads the same way. No assertion, generator, case count or input domain changed anywhere. crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs hoists the two now-allocating accessors out of the iterator chains as reads_now and never_read, so each is called once instead of once per kept row, which avoids the quadratic allocation the method change could otherwise have introduced on the resume path. The mutation measurement I asked for was made by the owner, not by me: deleting the admits arm of the two pre-existing faults makes review_app_scan_store_failure exit 101 with 2 of 4 failing on completed instead of interrupted, and the arm was restored. That is the kill I judged by reading the two test bodies, now measured; I did not re-perform it, because constructing the mutant means editing candidate production bytes, which this role may not do, so its provenance is the owner's run and the tree I observed is the restored one, clean at ea8f6d9.

diagnostic: Accepted at HEAD ea8f6d9 with no finding open. All five findings of the previous round are resolved, each by its own owner in its own artifact, and every check is green on the whole workspace. Re-executed at HEAD, nothing reused because three production crates changed: the S1 oracle suite, exit 0, 11 passed; review-domain with adapter-review-store and ports, exit 0, 265 passed over 11 binaries; cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins, the corrected command 6, exit 0, 39 passed; cargo xtask check-arch, exit 0, OK over 30 workspace members; cargo test -p xtask, exit 0, 380 passed over 20 binaries; cargo check --release --workspace, exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, exit 0, no warning anywhere; the whole openlore-review-app package, exit 0, 322 passed over 22 binaries. No count moved, which is what a behaviour-preserving refactor and a documentation correction should show. The resolutions. Design: architecture.md command 6 is now --bins and runs, and the decision is docs/adrs/ADR-092 rather than the product ADR-001 path. Release seam: the Mutex, the ScanWriteSeam and the poisoned-lock error exist only under cfg(debug_assertions), a release build carries the uninhabited fault alone and reads the pure admits straight off the field, so the test seam costs a release build nothing and adds it no failure mode; the release workspace check compiles. Resume partition: the verdict is one private Vec of (position, Disposition) with a private sum type carrying the skip reason, and to_read, carried, already_read, skipped and kept are all derived over that single sequence, so the disjointness the count rests on moved from a property-tested invariant to a structural one, which is the strongest form the finding asked for; resume_plan is now a filter_map over a pure total disposition_of and kept needs no sort. Adopted properties: acceptance.md records both formerly producer-authored proptests as oracle locators at lines 449 and 483, each with its stimulus, expected observation, user value and an honest caveat, so all sixteen recorded locators now have one owner and no test in the candidate is unowned. Mutation: the owner measured the mutant I could only judge by reading, deleting the admits arm makes review_app_scan_store_failure exit 101 with 2 of 4 failing on completed instead of interrupted, and restored it; that provenance is the owner's run, not mine, and the tree I observed is the restored one. Every test edit this round is the field-to-method migration the refactor forces, with no assertion, generator, case count or input domain changed, and scan.rs hoists the two now-allocating accessors out of their iterator chains so the resume path does not become quadratic. Limitations retained: typesafe unavailable, exit 3, key absent from this process, so no service judgment is claimed anywhere in this review; this repository has no test-impact selector, so selection stayed mechanical from the touched paths throughout; no timing statement is made and no half-budget or derogation case arose; I constructed no mutant and performed no production edit.
